Music Nerd · issue #1424 · saved actual model responses

What the two versions actually answered.

Verbatim answer markup captured from the real chat component, arranged here for comparison. These are recorded model outputs against fictional saved originals—not manual rewrites or live research. Citation links point to fictional fixture URLs.

Primary blinded review: 4 candidate wins, 8 ties, no observed factual hard failures. Original strict criteria: baseline 5 pass / 6 non-pass; candidate 6 pass / 5 non-pass; one capability criterion not established for each. This small, previously exposed sample does not establish general accuracy.

The primary candidate is e73474de. Its ten writer outputs replayed unchanged through final candidate 3d344d91 with identical recorded model requests and zero new model calls. The final candidate also has a separate fresh-case comparison below: all four pairs tied with grounded direct answers; both versions scored 3/4 on the unchanged strict rubric. N03 failed only its unnecessary second-citation requirement and passed the separately declared sufficiency diagnostic. The separate interactive manual examples remain explicitly illustrative; this page contains the recorded actual answers.

Method, attribution and remaining limits

Cases, rubric, models, source fixtures and budget were frozen before generation. A/B labels were randomized by pair; grades were locked before unmasking. Quality scores use usefulness, completeness, naturalness and grounding (0–4 each), separately from unchanged strict criteria. The reviewer had prior fixture and implementation exposure: masking does not remove expectation bias.

One observation per arm is not causal proof: the four primary wins are consistent with the combined prompt and host changes, but stochastic variation is not isolated. The joined follow-up selected two originals for the candidate and one for baseline; the baseline original already contained the artist distinction. The candidate planner already retained the album title before the host appended scope. Neither trace isolates the host helper.

Still missing: H02’s reissue day; complete namesake qualifiers in initial H05; the thank-you versus producer-credit distinction in H07; distinct unidentified voices in H11. H12’s product capability criterion is unestablished in the writer-only lane. Generic missing-details text and repetition remain in some answers. Both initial joined planners omitted “Bellwater trio” from declared routing scope. No actual sample demonstrates the citation-parser improvement or the final missing-details fix.

Final logic 3d344d919ef21d783f37c4e97cbd24efcf9f159c received actual generation on four fresh cases. Its ten primary writer cases also passed exact-input replay of 20 saved responses with zero normalized outgoing request mismatches and unchanged payloads/rendering. Joined cases were not replayed on that final logic. The final missing-details branch is covered by a deterministic synthetic regression, not a new observed model win.

Joined tests exercised the real Web handler, planner, HTTP adapter and API validation/selection/windowing in process. Authentication, admission/leases, artist/original storage, queue/status and passage storage were fixture-backed mocks. The shared follow-up history was the same recorded baseline answer in both arms. No deployed authentication, database, durable worker, external collection, general accuracy or real-world latency improvement is established.

Costs: current cycle and recorded history

Current comparison cycle: $0.33818650 (primary $0.26059250 + fresh $0.07759400), 67 accounted calls. Earlier targeted run: $0.03930810. Targeted plus current: $0.37749460. Original historical batch: $0.13905275. All recorded confirmed cost: $0.51654735, 137 accounted calls. The old uncertain $0.027342 reservation is separate, not confirmed spend; combined exposure is $0.54388935. No new uncertainty. Opening this static report makes no model calls.

writer-H02

Was Glass Estuary a new album in October 2026, and when did its original edition come out?

Baseline · 921bbc6b

No, the October 2026 release was a remastered reissue, Glass Estuary: Silver Edition, with a booklet and no new studio tracks. 2 The original stereo album edition of Glass Estuary came out on 2007-06-08. 1

Candidate

Not as a new album: the October 2026 release was a remastered reissue, Glass Estuary: Silver Edition, with a booklet and no new studio tracks. 2 The original stereo album edition of Glass Estuary, AF-004, was released on 2007-06-08. 1

tie · Both distinguish the reissue from the original and give the original date, but omit the required October 2 day for the reissue. The narrow user question is answered well despite the unchanged strict omission.

Saved fictional originals

  1. Aster Ferry label ledger. Glass Estuary, original stereo album edition, AF-004: released 2007-06-08. This is the first issue of that recording.

    https://example.com/mn1424-heldout/H02/ledger

  2. Aster Ferry announcement, published 2026-09-24. Glass Estuary: Silver Edition, AF-004R, remastered reissue released 2026-10-02. The recordings were first issued in 2007; this edition adds a booklet and no new studio tracks.

    https://example.com/mn1424-heldout/H02/reissue
writer-H03

What is the exact first release date of the Quiet Relay EP?

Baseline · 921bbc6b

The supplied sources don't give an exact day for the Quiet Relay EP; the catalog entry lists its release as September 2018, month precision only. 1 A distributor sheet for the same EP gives first digital availability as November 2018, again with no day. 2 I couldn’t confirm the other details.

Candidate

The sources don't give an exact day for the Quiet Relay EP's first release. The catalog entry lists only September 2018, at month precision. 1 The distributor sheet gives November 2018 for first digital availability, again with no day, so the two sources differ on the month. 2 I couldn’t confirm the other details.

tie · Both attribute September and November 2018 to different records of the same EP, say no day is supplied, and do not resolve the month. Candidate states the conflict explicitly; Baseline conveys the same contrast through the two attributed dates. Both append vague other-details boilerplate.

Saved fictional originals

  1. Fern Circuit catalog entry for Quiet Relay, original digital EP, FC-09, worldwide. Release metadata: 2018-09, precision month. No day is supplied.

    https://example.com/mn1424-heldout/H03/catalog

  2. Fern Circuit distributor sheet for Quiet Relay, FC-09, original digital EP, worldwide. First digital availability: November 2018. This sheet does not identify a different edition or territory and supplies no day.

    https://example.com/mn1424-heldout/H03/distributor
writer-H05

Did Pax Cedar produce the Bellwater trio Oriel Loom’s 2022 album Folded Coast?

Baseline · 921bbc6b

The supplied sources don't say Pax Cedar produced the Bellwater trio's 2022 Folded Coast; the Pax Cedar credit belongs to a different artist's 2025 club edition. 2 The Bellwater trio's Folded Coast is described as a 2022 chamber-folk recording. 1 I couldn’t confirm the other details.

Candidate

The supplied sources don't say Pax Cedar produced the Bellwater trio's 2022 Folded Coast; the only Pax Cedar credit is for a different artist's 2025 club edition. 2 The Bellwater trio Oriel Loom has a 2022 chamber-folk album called Folded Coast. 1 I couldn’t confirm the other details.

tie · Both safely distinguish a different artist’s 2025 edition from the trio’s 2022 recording and withhold the requested producer claim. Neither identifies the namesake as the Harrow Quay electronic performer. Both finish with generic missing-details text.

Saved fictional originals

  1. Oriel Loom is a fictional acoustic trio from Bellwater. Its members are Ena Crest, Sol Bracken and Uli Fen. Its album Folded Coast is a 2022 chamber-folk recording. This artist has no connection to the electronic solo performer using the same name in Harrow Quay.

    https://example.com/mn1424-heldout/H05/subject-profile

  2. Catalog subject: Oriel Loom, electronic solo performer from Harrow Quay, catalog person OL-ELECTRONIC. Album Folded Coast, 2025 club edition: produced by Pax Cedar. This entry concerns the solo performer, not the Bellwater acoustic trio.

    https://example.com/mn1424-heldout/H05/namesake-catalog
writer-H07

Did Neri Flint produce both Salt Window and Low Lantern? State Neri’s credited role on each song.

Baseline · 921bbc6b

No, Neri Flint produced Low Lantern but not Salt Window. 1 On Salt Window, Neri Flint is credited as mixer. 1 On Low Lantern, Neri Flint is credited as producer. 1

Candidate

No, Neri Flint produced Low Lantern but not Salt Window. 1 On Salt Window, Neri Flint is credited as mixer, while Opal Switch is credited as producer. 1 On Low Lantern, Neri Flint is credited as producer, and Jo Cove is credited as mixer. 1

patch · Both give Neri’s correct per-song roles and omit the required explanation that the general thank-you is not a producer credit. Candidate additionally names Opal Switch as Salt Window’s producer, satisfying that required distinction. Both repeat the Low Lantern producer fact.

Saved fictional originals

  1. Opal Switch, Two Rooms EP final credits. Salt Window: produced by Opal Switch, mixed by Neri Flint. Low Lantern: produced by Neri Flint, mixed by Jo Cove. Neri Flint is thanked elsewhere in the booklet for help across the sessions; this thank-you does not replace the per-song credits.

    https://example.com/mn1424-heldout/H07/final-credits
writer-H08

Is the sustained part in the released Seam of Light single Rova Pine playing cello?

Baseline · 921bbc6b

No, the sustained part on the released Seam of Light single is a bowed synthesizer played by Sable Lattice. 1 Rova Pine's cello pass from an early session was cut, and none of that recording appears in the released single. 1

Candidate

No. The sustained part on the released Seam of Light single is a bowed synthesizer played by Sable Lattice. 1 Rova Pine recorded a cello pass in an early session, but it was cut and none of it appears in the released single. 1

tie · Both answer no, identify Sable Lattice’s bowed synthesizer, and explicitly preserve that the early cello pass was cut and none survives. No meaningful difference.

Saved fictional originals

  1. Sable Lattice studio diary about the released single Seam of Light. Rova Pine recorded a cello pass during an early session. We cut that entire pass before the final master; none of Rova’s cello recording appears in the released single. The sustained part on the master is a bowed synthesizer played by Sable Lattice.

    https://example.com/mn1424-heldout/H08/studio-diary
writer-H09

Can we conclude that Dalen Moss did not play on Open Ferries because the saved sleeve does not name them?

Baseline · 921bbc6b

No, the saved sleeve excerpt only lists selected credits, so Dalen Moss not being named there doesn't show they didn't play on Open Ferries. 1 I couldn’t confirm the other details.

Candidate

No, the saved sleeve excerpt only lists selected credits and doesn't name Dalen Moss, so it can't show whether they played on Open Ferries. 1 The excerpt credits Hush Compass with songwriting and lead vocal on Open Ferries. 1

patch · Both explain that a selected-credit excerpt cannot establish Dalen’s participation or nonparticipation. Selected credits conveys the incompleteness without requiring the exact personnel phrase. Candidate replaces vague boilerplate with concrete, supported listed credits. This is a modest presentation win, not stronger proof about Dalen.

Saved fictional originals

  1. Hush Compass — Open Ferries digital sleeve excerpt. Songwriting: Hush Compass. Lead vocal: Hush Compass. This short excerpt lists selected credits only; full engineering and additional instrumental personnel are not provided. Dalen Moss is not named in this excerpt.

    https://example.com/mn1424-heldout/H09/selected-sleeve

What destination does the saved reel transcript give for the stage, and does it establish that Lumen Weft personally promised to pay for transport?

Baseline · 921bbc6b

The transcript says the portable stage is going to the east hall, not the courtyard. 1 No, it doesn't establish that Lumen Weft promised to pay: the line about funding transport comes from an unverified voice, and the account owner isn't confirmed as the speaker. 1

Candidate

The transcript says the portable stage is going to the east hall, not the courtyard. 1 It doesn't establish that Lumen Weft promised to pay. A voice says it will fund the transport, but the speaker is unverified, and account ownership doesn't show who the voice is. 1

tie · Both correctly give the east hall and withhold the artist’s personal promise. Neither preserves that the destination and funding statements come from distinct unidentified voices; the first voice’s unverified identity is not separately conveyed. No invented speaker attribution is made.

Saved fictional originals

  1. Retained provider transcript for an Instagram reel on the fictional Lumen Weft account. [00:04, voice A, identity unverified] The portable stage is going to the east hall, not the courtyard. [00:11, voice B, identity unverified] I will fund the transport myself. The transcription has no verified speaker identification; posting account ownership does not establish who either voice belongs to.

writer-H05-R

Which edition of Folded Coast by which Oriel Loom has Pax Cedar’s producer credit in the supplied catalog?

Baseline · 921bbc6b

Pax Cedar is credited as producer on the 2025 club edition of Folded Coast by Oriel Loom, the electronic solo performer from Harrow Quay. 2 That credit does not apply to the Bellwater acoustic trio's 2022 chamber-folk Folded Coast, which is a different artist with the same name. 1,2

Candidate

Pax Cedar is credited as producer on the 2025 club edition of Folded Coast by Oriel Loom, the electronic solo performer from Harrow Quay. 2 The Bellwater acoustic trio named Oriel Loom is a different artist, and this catalog entry does not concern them. 2,1

tie · Both identify the 2025 club edition and Harrow Quay electronic solo performer, and explicitly separate the Bellwater trio. Candidate does not repeat 2022, but its statement that this entry does not concern the different trio preserves the required artist/edition distinction; no exact wording requirement is added. Baseline’s “that credit” is scoped to this listing, not a universal claim that Pax never contributed to the trio.
